artifact: You keep a result in a cache so you can reuse it. But if the underlying data changes before that copy is removed or refreshed, you may be using a stale result. Cache invalidation addresses that gap: its rule decides when to remove or refresh the cached copy. Here, we are following one cache; coordinating changes across multiple services is outside this scenario.
